faq.q: What kinds of graphs can I plot, and what syntax does it accept?
faq.a: Three modes: Cartesian y=f(x) with multiple functions on one graph, Polar r=f(θ) over a chosen number of full turns, and Parametric x(t)/y(t) over a t range. Expressions use + - * / ^, parentheses, and functions like sin, cos, tan, asin, log (base 10), ln, exp, sqrt, abs, floor, pow, plus the constants pi and e. Example: sin(x) + x^2/4.

faq.q: Are the trig functions in degrees or radians?
faq.a: Radians. This is the single most common plotting mistake: sin(30) is the sine of 30 radians (about −0.988), not 0.5. To work in degrees, convert by multiplying by pi/180 inside your expression, for example sin(x*pi/180).

faq.q: Does it do calculus, like derivatives and integrals?
faq.a: Yes, for Cartesian functions. Pick which function to analyse, then tick 'Plot derivative' (computed numerically via a central difference) or 'Shade integral' between a chosen a and b — the area is estimated with a 1000-step midpoint rule and shown as '∫ ... ≈ value'. Trace mode also marks roots, the y-intercept and local maxima/minima, and reads out coordinates under the cursor.

faq.q: Can I get the plotted values as numbers or save my work?
faq.a: Yes. The 'Table of Values' tool tabulates a function over an x-range and step (up to 500 rows), and you can copy it as CSV or as TSV for pasting into a spreadsheet, or copy a text analysis summary. Export the graph itself as a PNG. Your functions, ranges and view settings autosave to local storage under graphPlotter.state, and 'Clear saved state' resets them.
